beforeRecord.q: In the identity public saving = T − G, what must T represent in this accounting framework?
options: Net tax revenue after relevant transfers
Total federal outlays including transfers and net interest
Gross tax collections before subtracting any transfer payments
The accumulated federal debt stock at a specific date
beforeRecord.commonError: Incorrectly concludes “Total federal outlays including transfers and net interest” in this budget accounting and public saving task.
beforeRecord.feedback: The shorthand is valid here only when T is defined net of transfers and G is government purchases.

afterRecord.q: Public saving equals T − G, where G is government purchases. How should T account for transfer payments?
options: Net tax revenue after relevant transfers
Total federal outlays including transfers and net interest
Gross tax collections before subtracting any transfer payments
The accumulated federal debt stock at a specific date
afterRecord.commonError: Incorrectly concludes “Total federal outlays including transfers and net interest” in this budget accounting and public saving task.
afterRecord.feedback: T is tax revenue minus transfer payments. Public saving is therefore taxes minus transfers minus government purchases.

rationale: Natural, explicit wording from instructor review

beforeRecord.q: Under public saving = T − G, with T defined as net tax revenue and G as government purchases, what does negative public saving mean?
options: Private saving must also be below zero
T is less than G
Nominal GDP must be declining during the year
The government can have no outstanding federal debt
beforeRecord.commonError: Incorrectly concludes “Private saving must also be below zero” in this budget accounting and public saving task.
beforeRecord.feedback: Public saving is negative when net tax revenue T is below government purchases G.

afterRecord.q: Government purchases exceed tax revenue after transfer payments have been subtracted. If T is that net tax revenue and G is government purchases, which relationship explains why public saving is negative?
options: Private saving must also be below zero
T is less than G
Nominal GDP must be declining during the year
The government can have no outstanding federal debt
afterRecord.commonError: Incorrectly concludes “Private saving must also be below zero” in this budget accounting and public saving task.
afterRecord.feedback: Public saving is negative when net tax revenue T is below government purchases G.

rationale: Natural, explicit wording from instructor review

options: Public saving is necessarily higher

afterRecord.commonError: Incorrectly concludes “Government purchases are no longer part of GDP” in this budget accounting and public saving task.
afterRecord.feedback: A larger deficit means the government saves less or borrows more, reducing public saving.

beforeRecord.q: A legislature authorizes $120 million of spending while the central bank adjusts its monetary stance. Which accountability distinction is valid?
options: The central bank writes the spending appropriation whenever monetary policy is independent
Independence means the central bank has no legal mandate or reporting obligation
The Treasury must approve every private bank loan because it authorizes public spending
Fiscal authorities authorize spending; the central bank implements monetary policy under its legal mandate and accountability framework
beforeRecord.commonError: Incorrectly concludes “The central bank writes the spending appropriation whenever monetary policy is independent” in this central bank and federal reserve task.
beforeRecord.feedback: Institutional separation distinguishes fiscal appropriations from monetary policy. Operational independence is compatible with a legislated mandate and accountability, not an absence of constraints.

afterRecord.q: The legislature approves government spending while the central bank changes interest rates. Which statement correctly describes their responsibilities?
options: The central bank approves public spending; the legislature sets monetary policy.
The legislature approves public spending; the central bank operates without legal obligations.
The legislature approves public spending; the Treasury must approve every private bank loan.
The legislature approves public spending; the central bank conducts monetary policy under its legal mandate.
afterRecord.commonError: Incorrectly concludes “The central bank writes the spending appropriation whenever monetary policy is independent” in this central bank and federal reserve task.
afterRecord.feedback: The legislature authorizes public spending. The central bank conducts monetary policy within its legal mandate and remains accountable for its actions.

beforeRecord.q: At the efficient quantity:
options: All buyers get equal surplus
All sellers have equal costs
The price is morally fair
The last unit’s value equals its cost.
beforeRecord.feedback: Under the standard competitive model, efficiency is determined at the margin: the last unit’s value equals its cost.

afterRecord.q: In a competitive market with no externalities, what is true of the last unit produced at the quantity that maximizes total surplus?
options: All buyers get equal surplus
All sellers have equal costs
The price is morally fair
The last unit’s value equals its cost.
afterRecord.feedback: At the efficient quantity, the last unit’s marginal benefit equals its marginal cost. Producing less leaves gains from trade unrealized; producing more costs more than buyers value those additional units.

options: Public saving falls, supply shifts left, and the real rate rises

Consumption falls, demand shifts left, and the rate falls

beforeRecord.q: Why is 'a deficit eliminates all private investment' too strong?
options: Crowding out means investment is lower than otherwise, not necessarily zero
Deficits always reduce the real interest rate
Public saving is unrelated to national saving
Investment demand becomes perfectly vertical
beforeRecord.commonError: Incorrectly concludes “Deficits always reduce the real interest rate” in this crowding out and capital formation task.
beforeRecord.feedback: The market mechanism reduces equilibrium investment relative to its counterfactual level; the size depends on curves and the saving change.

afterRecord.q: Why can a government budget deficit reduce private investment without eliminating it?
options: Crowding out means investment is lower than otherwise, not necessarily zero
Deficits always reduce the real interest rate
Public saving is unrelated to national saving
Investment demand becomes perfectly vertical
afterRecord.commonError: Incorrectly concludes “Deficits always reduce the real interest rate” in this crowding out and capital formation task.
afterRecord.feedback: Crowding out means investment falls relative to what it would otherwise have been. Higher interest rates can discourage some projects while others remain profitable.

rationale: Natural, explicit wording from instructor review

beforeRecord.q: If private investment is $30 billion lower because of crowding out, what is the careful growth implication?
options: The existing capital stock immediately falls by $30 billion
Capital formation is lower than it otherwise would be
Long-run output must fall by exactly $30 billion
All future economic growth stops
beforeRecord.commonError: Incorrectly concludes “The existing capital stock immediately falls by $30 billion” in this crowding out and capital formation task.
beforeRecord.feedback: Crowding out reduces the flow of new capital investment relative to the counterfactual; it does not mechanically erase existing capital.

afterRecord.q: Crowding out reduces private investment by $30 billion. What does this imply for the economy’s capital formation?
options: The existing capital stock immediately falls by $30 billion
Capital formation is lower than it otherwise would be
Long-run output must fall by exactly $30 billion
All future economic growth stops
afterRecord.commonError: Incorrectly concludes “The existing capital stock immediately falls by $30 billion” in this crowding out and capital formation task.
afterRecord.feedback: The economy adds less new capital than it otherwise would. A reduction in new investment does not itself remove existing capital.

rationale: Natural, explicit wording from instructor review

A larger budget surplus with no rate change

beforeRecord.feedback: With the stock held fixed, a higher effective rate raises the interest paid during the year.

beforeRecord.q: Inflation falls from 8% to 3%, and later to −1%. How does the price level change at 3% inflation and at −1% inflation?
options: Prices rise in both periods; the sign of the inflation rate affects only unemployment.
At 3% prices still rise; at −1% they fall, so only the latter is deflation.
At 3% prices fall; at −1% they rise, so only the former is deflation.

beforeRecord.feedback: Disinflation is a reduction in inflation. A still-positive rate means a rising price level; a negative rate means a falling price level. Crossing zero therefore changes the direction of prices even though inflation fell in both transitions.
